text:
Lowest-cost plan I found: 6 periods at $94.94 total, missing 4 of the 42 (episode, Wen) pairs. I don't think zero misses is possible, and I believe 4 is the minimum, but that is not exhaustively proven.

**Why some misses are unavoidable**

All three services Wen follows release episodes from mid-December to late February, but only 2 can be active at once. Tidewell isn't needed.

- Kestrel+ must be on by Dec 30 to catch episode 1 (window Dec 23–30).
- A Kestrel+ month that starts by Dec 30 holds one slot for about 31 days.
- During that month, Marquee and Lumen must share the other slot. Each can be off only about 10–13 days without missing an episode.
- So in late December and January, some service must be off long enough to miss episodes.
- Every month-long block of one service forces the other two to share, and the gap lengths end up nearly fixed. With the best date alignment, I found no arrangement below 4 misses.

**The plan**

| Service | Paid period | Episodes missed |
|---|---|---|
| Marquee | Nov 28 – Dec 27 | — |
| Lumen | Dec 17 – Jan 16 | — |
| Kestrel+ | Dec 28 – Jan 27 | — |
| Marquee | Jan 17 – Feb 16 | — |
| Lumen | Jan 28 – Feb 27 | — |
| Kestrel+ | Feb 17 – Mar 16 | — |

Gaps between periods cause these misses:
- **Marquee**, off Dec 28 – Jan 16: misses The Crooked Tide episodes 3 and 4 (Dec 29 and Jan 5).
- **Lumen**, off Jan 17 – Jan 27: misses The Paper Ferry episode 6 (Jan 17).
- **Kestrel+**, off Jan 28 – Feb 16: misses The Salt Meridian episode 7 (Feb 3).

**Checks**
- **Never more than 2 at once:** In late November only Marquee is active, because the already-paid access has ended by Nov 28. After that, exactly two services are active each day.
- **No double payment:** Every period starts after that service's paid-through date, and periods of the same service don't overlap.
- **Dates:** All starts fall inside Nov 1 – Apr 30. None falls on the 29th–31st, so every end date is well defined.
- **Cost:** Each service needs at least 2 months to cover its release span, so 6 periods is the minimum. That gives 2 × ($17.99 + $13.99 + $15.49) = **$94.94**.
